documentation.02c55f87: Yes. What the generator writes is original by construction: it was assembled from rules and a number, with no recording anywhere in the chain, so there is nothing in it that came from somebody else's work. You own your output and you do not owe anything to anyone for it — see the licence below for the exact wording.
documentation.0969199e: Mute and solo are preview controls. They change what you hear and never the song or the exported file — the same distinction the per-lane audio mute draws. documentation.0a36b11f: The browser can take the whole rail when you need the depth, and hand it back. Audio and MIDI are kept apart on purpose: a .mid has no waveform to draw and cannot be dropped on a drum pad, and the pad refuses it before you let go rather than failing afterwards.
documentation.0b27ac6b: Crash reports are written to a folder on your own disk and are never sent anywhere. They exist so you have something to attach to a bug report if you choose to — nothing reads that folder but you.

documentation.1125e7e4: A pin is held inside the range the artist works in. The BPM box stops at the range shown in the panel — drag or type past it and it settles at the edge — and switching to an artist who cannot reach your pin brings it to their nearest tempo rather than generating something they never play. Typing is only corrected when you leave the box, so 1 on the way to 140 is not rewritten under your cursor. The host is never held to it: a project's tempo is the project's.
documentation.114f1c77: What if it accidentally writes a melody that already exists?
documentation.1223e0b4: It is kept per user rather than in the project — where you have been generating is a fact about you, not something to ship inside a song sent to a label — and it survives an update. Each artist keeps its own run of takes, so an evening spent on one cannot push out the ones you saved from another. Clear it whenever you like: it is a record of what you have been making, and being able to empty it is not a convenience.
documentation.13e89cca: Choosing a take restores it, the same as the arrows do — so anything you have drawn by hand on the current clip is replaced. It is not a preview.
documentation.15955a81: Your pin wins. Pin a tempo in the session chips and it beats everything.

documentation.1d3f4df2: The ordinary caveat applies and has nothing to do with this software: if you drop a sample you do not have the rights to onto a pad, that sample is still not yours. The notes are yours; a recording you imported is whatever it already was.
documentation.1f04dbe6: Two of these rows are verified and three are not. Ableton Live 12 and FL Studio have been loaded and generated in; Reaper, Bitwig and Logic have not been opened yet, so their rows describe what each host documents rather than what anyone has watched happen. documentation.21e024db: Inside a place, the arrows above the list walk the folders and the breadcrumb jumps straight to a level. Your library comes back next time you open the app, with or without a project.
documentation.22b5f3cc: Star the takes you like as you go. At thirty kept, Train fits a style to them — how many onsets a bar, what register, what shape the line made — and writes those ranges back as an ordinary style model. Your own .mid files can be training material too.

documentation.2458a52d: No, and not in the weak sense of "we do not call it that". There is no machine learning anywhere in the product — no model, no training data, no inference, no neural network of any kind. The engine reads a set of hand-written numbers and rules and builds a pattern from a seeded random generator. You can read those numbers: they are plain JSON, and every one of them is a tempo range, a swing percentage, a note density, a roll grammar or a chord tendency.
documentation.24a78f85: The transport plays whichever tab you are looking at. There is one schedule: the Song tab puts the whole arrangement on it, and going back to a generator tab hands it back that tab's clip. So the marker you can see is always the one that is moving.
documentation.2528b54c: Five part generators, plus Song Mode. Song Mode is not a sixth generator — it lays out an arrangement and fills the other five in.
documentation.25c81dca: If you would rather your own instrument played the notes, route the plugin's MIDI output to it the way your host does that, and turn the part's own sound off by leaving no instrument assigned to it.
documentation.2c40e200: The pattern itself is not stored — the inputs are, and the engine is deterministic, so restoring is a regeneration. That is why a saved project costs bytes instead of hundreds of kilobytes of notes.
documentation.2c807357: For a workflow that wants it. Integer only — AIFF has no float form here.
documentation.2d0fa842: Toggle it from any tab. Click and drag across the keys — how high up the key you press sets the velocity — or use the typing bed. The typing bed stands down while a text field has focus, so searching for an artist does not play notes at you.
documentation.2e81e526: That last line matters more than it looks. An artist who does not write countermelodies answers that tab with silence, correctly — they do not write them, so nothing is invented for them. Before the pane said so, the only way to find out was to press Generate and stare at an empty roll.
documentation.30e94467: A loop you drag into your DAW is always a 16-bit WAV, whatever this is set to. A dragged loop has to carry its own tempo so it lands warped to the right speed instead of your project's, and only a WAV can hold that. This setting is for files you save, where you chose the destination.
documentation.30f4f34e: Play any slot to hear it. Swap re-rolls one slot without touching the others, × removes one, and Export writes whatever is left — with an optional normalize. The render happens in the background with a progress bar and a Cancel, so your DAW's window never stops drawing.
documentation.32319078: Then the host. With auto-sync on, the DAW's tempo is used.
documentation.33491a5d: Star anything — a sample, a one-shot or a MIDI file. The star sits to the left of the name: an outline until you press it, then solid yellow. Starred files gather in a list under the tree, and clicking one opens every folder between the root and that file to reveal it. If its folder is no longer one you have added, it opens the file's location in Windows Explorer or Finder instead — so a favourite is reachable whatever your library has moved on to. Unstarring forgets it.
documentation.34ccd0a3: Keeps anything that went past full scale, so a hot bounce can still be pulled back down.
documentation.3bf82a34: So how can it sound like a specific artist?
documentation.3de3cadc: Hear it first. Select a .mid and the panel lists what is inside it; press Play and it sounds — through a plain built-in instrument rather than whichever artist you happen to have selected, so the same file sounds the same tomorrow. Drum lanes come through as hits rather than as pitches, because a drum lane's note number says which pad fires, not how low it is. It is built on the first press, not when you click the file, so walking a folder of loops with ↓ costs nothing. It never touches your project's transport.
documentation.3df20937: A dragged audio loop carries its own tempo, so it lands warped to the speed it was made at rather than to your project's. That is a WAV thing specifically, which is why a dragged loop is always a 16-bit WAV whatever the export format is set to.
documentation.3e527f79: Every shortcut the plugin and the standalone have, grouped the way the in-app panel groups them. Press <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>?</kbd> in the app to see the same list with your own remappings, which this page cannot know about.
documentation.3fb1265f: Settings → MIDI input, below the input settings — both are about what crosses between this plugin and your own gear. WAV or AIFF, 16-bit, 24-bit or 32-bit float, at 44.1, 48, 88.2, 96, 176.4 or 192 kHz.
documentation.40db79d3: The number on a row is the whole shelf, not what survived the filters, so it does not move when you press a chip. The rows read in alphabetical order in whichever of the eighteen languages you are using. A folder whose drive is unplugged keeps its place and is marked Unavailable in words rather than only in a colour, and it stays removable — a producer who unplugged their sample disk has not left the library.
documentation.410bfc53: Collaboration is the one exception, and only if you use it. Rooms connect your machine directly to the people you invite. If you save someone as a buddy, a small service can tell you when they are online — and it is told nothing worth knowing: a key that changes every few minutes, and an address encrypted to a secret only the two of you hold. It cannot read it, cannot list who is there, and cannot work out who knows whom. Turn it off, or never save a buddy, and you paste a code instead. The collaboration service is reached by a separate program, never by the plugin your DAW loads, which is what keeps the sentence above true.
documentation.421a3d31: "Trained" means fitted, and there is no machine learning anywhere in it. Nothing is learned from anybody else's music, nothing leaves your machine, and a fit that would only repeat itself is refused with a reason rather than saved. The floor of thirty exists so a style encodes your taste rather than one seed's opinion.
documentation.462f801c: <kbd>R</kbd>, or the dice on the section header. Locked clips are left alone
documentation.4a4148dd: The filter, both envelopes, the effects and the master controls for whichever generator you are shaping. The four buttons at the top choose which one — the SYNTH tab is the only tab that is not itself a part, so it has to ask.
documentation.4d68e35d: A note transposed past the ends of the keyboard is dropped, not wrapped. A wrapped note is a wrong note, and nothing on screen would tell you it happened.
documentation.4df575be: Name a pattern you like and it is there next time — in any song, in any DAW. Each one is its own JSON file in the platform's per-user data directory, so a bad save costs one loop rather than the shelf, and you can back them up, sync them, or hand one to someone else by copying a file.
documentation.4e322996: An artist only offers moods that artist actually does. Moods are inherited down the same lineage as everything else, so there is no path by which one artist's mood could be offered on another. Ask for one a style does not have and it says so by name rather than quietly generating something else.
documentation.4ec1e842: One multi-track .mid, or one file per part into a folder
documentation.4ec55525: If the interface is what broke, you will see a panel with a way back into your session rather than a dead rectangle — the arrangement lives outside the part that crashed, so pressing the button redraws your own work. Report it anyway; the log is already on disk.
documentation.4f2277e8: You find them with one type-to-autocomplete box. Start typing and it narrows as you go — across the mainstream roster, the underground roster, aliases, and typos. Stop halfway and click away and it takes the best match, so you can never be left with nothing chosen. Press the arrow instead and it shows you everything.
documentation.5415794a: Lock a lane and a re-roll cannot touch it. Click the padlock on any drum row, or press L with the row focused, and Generate rebuilds everything else around it note for note. A lock changes nothing about what is exported.

documentation.5811086b: It holds a real library. A folder with two thousand files in it opens as fast as one with four, because only the rows you can actually see are drawn — scroll and the rest arrive as you reach them. Type in the filter box and the tree narrows to what matches, keeping the folders that lead to it; type a folder's name and you get everything under it. The line beneath the box says which folders were searched, and it means it: the plugin reads one folder at a time, so the filter reaches the ones you have opened and no further. A box that implied otherwise would be lying about what it looked at.
documentation.58c0f8e2: No accounts. No telemetry. Nothing about you, your projects or your output is transmitted. Generation, playback, import and export are entirely local.
documentation.58fc0ea4: Where did the drum loops and the one-shots come from?
documentation.5acc0069: Pitches are chosen as scale degrees and only then turned into MIDI notes, so staying in key is structural rather than filtered for afterwards.
documentation.5d19dc54: A preset is a named session — artist, seed, bars and pins. Factory presets are compiled into the binary; your own are written to the platform's per-user data directory, so they outlive any one project.
documentation.5d361274: The music you make with it is yours, with no royalty and no attribution requirement.
documentation.5d689d19: Eight pads sit across the top of the stage, above the piano roll. Each one is a drum lane: its name, what is currently on it, and a dot saying whether you can hear it — green for audible, red for muted.
documentation.5d91da4a: Choose a folder and get one file per part — MIDI, or audio in whichever format you set. This is the road that works on every platform, and the one to use for a whole arrangement.
documentation.5e24a1af: Then the artist. With auto-sync off, the model's own authored tempo stands.
documentation.6034b304: Clicking a row plays it and nothing more. The clip you hear is the instrument at the note it sounds most like itself on, drawn as a waveform in the preview player under the browser, with a playhead and a running time. ↑ and ↓ walk the list and play whatever they land on, so you can hear your way through a family without touching the mouse.
documentation.6053a251: A saved pattern is notes, not sound. The kit is deliberately not stored, which is what makes “use it with any sounds you want” true rather than a claim: load the pattern, swap the kit, and the same performance plays through different samples. It is also how a pattern survives a crash — a plugin lives in someone else's process and dies with it.
documentation.6324e27a: The arrow keys walk it. ↑ and ↓ move between rows. On a folder, → opens it and ← shuts it — and on an already-shut folder ← shuts the branch it sits in, so it is a way back out. On a file, those same two keys play it forwards and backwards. Auditioning never starts or stops the transport.
documentation.638c602e: Auto-sync is a session setting saved with your project — three states, not two. Turning it off is how you reach the artist's authored tempo from inside a running project.
documentation.63fa26a1: It inherits everything you did not change, including improvements the artist you based it on gets in a later release. A new style opens seeded from the beat on screen rather than from a blank form.

documentation.6c29a0d2: No factory preset pins a tempo. A pin is an instruction from the user, and a shipped file is not the user — a factory preset that pinned one would override your DAW the moment you loaded it.
documentation.6ce283a3: What most producers expect from a bounce. Six more dB of usable range.
documentation.6d222977: Every answer here is a restatement of something already written down in the licence, the name disclaimer or the credits. Nothing on this page is a new promise.
documentation.6d9aaa02: An arrangement that fills the five above in — a mode, not a generator
documentation.6dae90a7: The plugin makes no outbound connections at all. The two that used to exist — a launch-time update check and an opt-in crash report — belonged to the desktop app and were removed with it. A plugin is installed and updated by whoever installs plugins, and no HTTP client is compiled into it. Two build gates check this on every commit rather than trusting the claim: one reads the dependency graph and fails if an HTTP client is linked at all, the other drives the real interface through a generation and fails if the browser attempts a single request off the machine.
documentation.70a577ec: Your samples are only copied if you say so. A style can keep the one-shots you assigned, so they still play after you move or delete the originals. That means a second copy on your drive, so the editor tells you how many files and how many megabytes before anything happens — and the box is unticked. Saving a style copies nothing on its own.
documentation.74b1c304: Dragging is Windows only for now. On macOS and Linux the chips do not offer it, because a control that cannot work is worse than one that is not there. Use Export instead — it produces the same files.
documentation.75928332: Pick a genre and an instrument, choose how many, and Generate. Up to 25 one-shots are rendered offline, each trimmed and fade-shaped so it does not click, with anything that came out near-silent thrown away before it reaches the rack.
documentation.772074f7: No. See Privacy & the network above for the full answer, including the two things that do touch a network and why: fetching the web app, and collaboration if you choose to use it.
documentation.7a1b9f14: Moving the octave or the range sends an all-notes-off, so a held note cannot be stranded by the keys under it changing.
documentation.7b266d93: A layered file is separated into bass, melody, countermelody, chords and drums, and every part says why it was routed where it was — "on the GM drum channel", "chords — notes overlap", "lowest voice", "from the file name". A wrong guess is one click to redirect rather than something you discover two bars in.
documentation.7c97bb07: Drums go to drums and instruments go to generators. A stock instrument is a synth patch and a drum lane plays one-shots, so the shortcut refuses the pairing rather than doing something surprising with it. Ctrl + ◀ plays a sample backwards in the preview and will not put it into a generator that way — reversing a note is the piano roll's job.
documentation.7d883e08: The plugin writes notes onto the track you inserted it on and makes the sound itself — the drums through its kit, and each melodic part through its own instrument. You do not have to route it anywhere to hear it.

documentation.874b0424: Notes you play in are yours. They are never analysed, never become part of a style, and never train anything — the same rule a MIDI file you import lives under.
documentation.876884a2: Where a row shows <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> / <kbd>⌘</kbd>, that means Ctrl (Windows/Linux) or ⌘ (macOS).
documentation.8b53323c: Original Workflow sits at the top of the left rail, above everything. Start from any artist or genre, adjust the tempo range, swing, hat density, melody density and scales, and save it under your own name. It appears in the roster marked Yours and generates, locks, re-rolls and exports exactly like a shipped artist — because it is the same kind of thing, in the same format.
documentation.8dc74fe7: The readout shows the tempo and key that were actually used, which is not always what you pinned: a beat made while your DAW sat at 92 was made at 92, and tempo changes the notes.
documentation.90d83808: The filename says which half went: -panic is the audio engine with a backtrace, -page is the interface, and on Windows -fault is a hardware fault such as an access violation. The newest twenty are kept, so the folder never grows without limit and you can attach the lot to a bug report.

documentation.920e6fd6: Stems come out as MIDI or as audio, per part or per lane. The audio half used to be impossible and the reason was measured rather than assumed: the shipped kit had no voice for the four melodic parts, so rendering them would have written four silent .wavs and called them stems. The kit covers every generated lane now, and your own one-shots cover the rest. A whole song still writes one .mid per part — rendering minutes of audio needs progress you can watch and a cancel you can press, which is a different job from rendering a four-bar loop.
documentation.92ebf1ef: Can I release what I make? Can I sell it?
documentation.9412c301: Because a producer's habits are describable. How often the hats double up, where the snare lands, whether the 808 slides and how far, which chord families turn up and which never do — that is written out by hand, from published interviews, technique articles and listening. It is the same kind of document as a drum lesson that teaches you a shuffle, and it works for the same reason.
documentation.967c5bf5: A section plays a looping clip. A sixteen-bar verse is a four-bar loop played four times, which is what every DAW's arrangement view draws. Sections of the same kind share one clip, because verse 1 and verse 2 are the same beat — the switch-up exists precisely because that is the rule.
documentation.98f5460e: Generate. The pattern is built for your project's tempo and key.
documentation.99bec605: The plugin saves your artist, seed, bars, pins and window size into the DAW's own project file. Reopen the song and the session comes back. There is no file to manage and no path to choose.
documentation.9acfff56: Drag a .mid from the browser onto a generator and its notes land there. Drop it on the Song tab instead and the whole file arrives as an arrangement — sections across the top, parts down the side — and clicking any cell opens that clip in its generator, exactly as drilling into a generated song does. Nothing you already have is overwritten until you choose a cell.
documentation.9b3b8f91: Double-click it. Your edits write back into the arrangement

documentation.9e84e0da: Being straight about what that covers. The table holds public-domain melodies — traditional, hymn and classical — because building it from anything else would mean this software carrying somebody else's notes, which is the one thing it must never do. So the screen catches an accidental quotation of a famous tune, which is worth catching. It is not the reason your output is original. That is everything in the two answers above.
documentation.9eccb298: The plugin emits MIDI onto the track it is on, and it also makes the sound itself — the drums through its kit and each melodic part through its own instrument. Press play in your DAW and you hear the beat without routing anything.
documentation.a1904ba7: There is no reporter that phones home, and there never will be. What there is instead is a folder: when either half of the plugin falls over, it writes what happened to your own disk, and you decide whether to send it.
documentation.a1eb5eff: Putting one on a generator is a separate press — the Use in… button under the list, or Ctrl/⌘ + ▶, both of which land on the tab you are looking at. Choosing an instrument clears the reverb, drive, gain and envelope the previous one was wearing, so what the generator plays is what the preview played. You should not have to reach for a knob to get the sound you just heard.
documentation.a74dbbef: macOS only. Logic reads neither CLAP nor VST3.
documentation.a812ebd9: The plugin and the standalone never needed a network in the first place. The web app fetches itself once and then works with the network switched off.
documentation.a84eb15c: The same box lists artists and genres together, each row saying which it is, so you never have to know in advance whether "UK Drill" is a person or a style. Pick one and its details appear directly underneath — era, the genres it works in, the tempo range and key it tends toward, its moods by name, and which parts it writes and which it does not — before you press Generate. Genres are a browse filter, not the unit of generation — though a genre is itself a real style model and generates in its own right.
documentation.a8d36300: Downloads open at 1.0. There is no installer, no beta and no preview build before then — a plugin that half-works inside somebody's session is worse than one that is not there, so it ships when the QA matrix is green on every host and every OS.
documentation.a9a17e79: Reverb, delay, drive, volume and pan for the part you are looking at, with the same numbers in the per-part editor in the right-hand rail. They are one set of controls shown twice, not two that have to be kept in step.
documentation.aaa1fd33: Every pad's lane name is itself a picker — swap any of the eight for any of the thirty-seven lanes the plugin has. Two pads may share a lane, so you can layer a snare; a third is refused. Your layout is remembered per artist, so coming back to a style you built restores the pads exactly as you left them, with the samples you assigned.
documentation.aac58205: Volume, pan and the envelope belong to the lane, so they work whether that part is playing a factory instrument or a one-shot of your own. Reverb, delay and drive are applied to the instrument's own effects, so they appear only when a factory sound is loaded — over your own sample there would be nothing for them to reach, and a control that changes nothing is worse than one that is not there.
documentation.ac411997: No. No artist, producer, label or publisher named in this software has endorsed, sponsored, approved, reviewed or is affiliated with it in any way. Their names appear as descriptive references to a recognisable style and nothing else — the same way a chord chart might be labelled "bossa nova". No name is used as a brand or as a badge of origin for this software or for anything it generates.
documentation.ac4e2b0c: Every generation has a seed. The same seed, artist and session always produce a byte-identical pattern — on any machine, on any day. Copy the seed from the chip, paste it back, and the beat returns.
documentation.ac9b6565: It makes the sound as well as the notes. A polyphonic synthesiser with a factory library of 225 instruments across 69 genres, and each of the four melodic generators plays its own — so assigning a different sound to Melody, Countermelody, Bassline and Chords gives you four voices at once, not one shared between them.
documentation.b0e455fd: An artist is not one sound. Beside the artist is a mood — trap's dark, bounce, melodic and minimal; boom bap's dusty, jazzy and hard; phonk's cowbell, memphis and brazilian. Leave it on Any and each press walks that artist's range; pin one and stay there.
documentation.ba47208c: Grab a part chip and drag it onto a track. You get a .mid by default, or audio if you switch the chip. Dragging the whole arrangement gives one file per part.
documentation.bb221e18: No. A style model holds no MIDI, no audio, no transcription of any recording and no melodic or lyrical content from any song. There is no feature that recreates a specific track, and there never will be — that is a permanent design decision rather than something not built yet.
documentation.bd3b5639: Shape an instrument, then save it under a category and a name you choose. They are listed under those categories on the SYNTH tab.
documentation.bef6f4df: The web app is delivered over the network; what you make is not. A page has to be fetched — the app itself, and the style data it generates from. That is the whole of it. Generation runs on your own machine, in your own browser; your beats, your seeds and anything you import stay there and are never uploaded. After one visit the tab works with the network switched off.
documentation.c076a592: The plugin reads the host's tempo and time signature every block. Trap authored at 140 comes out at 92 in a 92 BPM project — because a clip generated at the artist's tempo does not fit the song you asked for.
documentation.c1864be2: It cannot sync to your DAW, and it never will — there is no host, so there is nothing to sync to. A fixed tempo can be set on the command line, which exercises the same path, but real host tempo, meter and playhead need a real host.
documentation.c4de4112: A mood is the same author writing a different kind of record, which is how producers describe their own catalogue. It is applied before any generator runs, so every part honours it — there is no way for the drums to be in one mood and the melody in another.
documentation.c5ebdb97: Where the formats live, once 1.0 lands:
documentation.c67e0e46: Artist names are descriptive style references only. Nothing in the dataset is copied MIDI, sampled audio, or a transcription of anyone's record.
documentation.c6f3d453: This is not a preset and not the project. A preset is a starting point and stores no notes at all, because the engine regenerates them; the project remembers this song. A saved pattern is the take you kept.
documentation.c7b038df: Reads CLAP natively. A multi-track .mid lands on the playlist as separate channels.
documentation.c81554ab: Octave echo, bell echo, arpeggio, answer lick and sustained pad, placed in the melody's gaps
documentation.c902e125: Determinism is enforced by the test suite, not merely intended — it is also why a saved project can restore a beat without storing a single note.
documentation.ca18c184: Every generation of the session is kept, from the first, counted separately per generator. <kbd>◀</kbd> and <kbd>▶</kbd> walk them, and stepping back brings the whole setup: the artist, the mood, the seed, the bars and the pins — not just the number.
documentation.ca365831: Everything the plugin does, and how it decides what to play.
documentation.ccf41857: Both are ours. The 5,085 shipped MIDI loops were written by this product's own generators from its own style models — no loop was extracted from anybody's audio or MIDI. The preview one-shots are synthesized from oscillators and filtered noise, so there is no recorded material in them at all and no third-party licence attached to them.
documentation.cd05c2a9: So: when you report it, say which host, which format (CLAP or VST3) and which OS version, and attach the newest file from the folder above. If the crash took the whole DAW down, attach the log your DAW wrote as well — when the host dies there may be no window of ours left to write from.
documentation.ce4fa0e2: Takes both. Reaper asks how to import a multi-track file rather than guessing.
documentation.d174c5c9: The repeat icon on the header; the speaker and <kbd>S</kbd> on the row
documentation.d18ca618: Kick, snare and off-snare, clap, closed and open hats with roll grammar, ride, crash, tom, rim, snap, perc, shaker, tambourine, cowbell and woodblock — plus the sliding sub. Which of them an artist uses is part of that artist.
documentation.d25c3d2f: It opens on Categories — one row per place, each saying how much is in it, and you go into them. Instruments and the four Factory Expansions are the shelves of the built-in library; Drum Packs holds the eleven shipped kits and their 407 one-shots; Factory Packs holds the 5,085 MIDI loops, by pack. Under those sit + Add Folder and the folders you have added, by name.
documentation.d51e6c21: The padlock on the cell, the part row, or the section header
documentation.d544549e: Name your files and it will listen. A file called …-Bass.mid or …Drums.mid is taken at its word, because that is you saying what it is rather than the plugin guessing. This matters more than it sounds: an 808's MIDI note says which key fires the sample, not how low it sounds, so a bassline routinely sits in melody register and no measurement can tell it from a slow lead. The one thing that can is the name you gave it.
documentation.d604eafc: Undo is unlimited within a session and covers the artist, seed, bars, pins, each generation and the arrangement — one stack, whichever tab you are on. Inside a text field your system's own undo takes the shortcut, so the seed box can still un-type a character.
documentation.d72a5e39: Every address is a different sound. The twenty-four variations of one instrument in one genre tour that instrument's own range — how long a bar rings, how hard a hammer strikes, where a string is plucked — rather than rolling dice twenty-four times, and the genre reaches the model itself rather than a filter after it: a trap 808 rings and slides where a house kick is tight, and a jazz piano is softer-hammered than a metal one. All 2,729,088 are checked, by rendering them.
documentation.d7bad06c: And it outlives the session. Click the take counter — the “3 / 40” between the arrows — and every generation you have ever made is there, grouped by artist, each row saying how long it is, how fast, and when you made it. Pick one and it comes back. The arrows answer “back one”; this is for the beat from Tuesday night whose seed you never wrote down.
documentation.d7eb09d9: Progressions in the session's key and scale
documentation.d9b0f0a8: Reroll or keep. Every generation carries a seed you can copy back.
documentation.dd09491c: Open Instruments or one of the four Factory Expansions and you browse that shelf by genre and family — the genres read alphabetically and the list opens on Trap. It is paged: one genre with no family filter is 5,400 rows. The shelf narrows the list, so opening Factory Expansion 2 and then Keys shows that pack’s Keys instruments and not every Keys instrument in the product.
documentation.dd323d51: A re-roll stays inside the record. It keeps the mode the song was generated in, the tempo and key it was generated at, and any swing you pinned — and it leaves every other section, including a clone of the one you re-rolled, exactly as it was.
documentation.e1f3b866: Hear it. Press play in your DAW — the notes are already on the track.
documentation.e6225dc8: Live does not read CLAP. Drop a .mid onto a MIDI track; Live makes one clip per track from a multi-track file.
documentation.e667e4fb: Three roads, and which one you want depends on what you are doing. The plugin plays on its own track, drags files out, or exports them to a folder.
documentation.e77855ff: The default, and what this plugin has always written.
documentation.e79791f6: It screens for that. Every melody and countermelody is fingerprinted by its shape — the run of intervals and the gaps between them — and checked against a table of well-known melodies before you hear it. A match is thrown away and drawn again.
documentation.e8595ab4: Nothing here is a sample library. Every sound is generated from a small address — an instrument, a genre, a variation, an articulation and a tone — so the whole library is a handful of integers in your project file rather than gigabytes on your disk. Thirteen synthesis engines sit behind it: a violin is a bowed-string model and a Rhodes is a physical piano model, which is why their controls behave differently from a pad's.
documentation.e90cfbee: The same plugin, in its own window, with no DAW involved — useful for trying things quickly and for machines where you are not producing.
documentation.eb60a3b0: Press Generate on the Song tab and you get a whole arrangement: one of the artist's own song forms, a clip per part per section, and the transitions that make it read as a record — the beat or two of silence before a hook lands, a back-half switch-up, an outro that fades.
documentation.ecfc86d6: All five generate, and all five are editable. Drums has a pad grid; melody, countermelody, bassline and chords have a piano roll. A style whose 808 is its bassline says so rather than doubling it with a second low end.
documentation.edc824f0: You can drag a part straight onto a DAW track. Every generated part has a MIDI and an Audio handle in the right rail; turn on Per lane and the drum part becomes one handle per lane, so just the hats can go out on their own. The whole arrangement drags too, as MIDI. Files arrive named trap - Snare - 140 BPM - C# Minor, and the clip's own notes ride on the cursor so you can see what you picked up. Windows only so far — an HTML5 drag inside a plugin's webview is not an operating-system file drag, so each platform needs its own native drag source. macOS and Linux keep Export until theirs is written, and show no drag handle rather than one that drops nothing.
documentation.ee7a9278: Settings → MIDI input. A channel filter (or all channels, which is the default), transpose in semitones, an octave shift that stacks with it, the pitch-bend range, and a velocity curve — below the middle a light touch comes out louder, above it you have to press harder.
documentation.f2eb4b94: The scale chip offers the scales that artist writes in. A mode is what carries their character, so a scale picked on one artist is handed back to the model when you move to another who does not use it. The key chip is deliberately not restricted — a key is transposition, the same music at another pitch.
documentation.f3887844: Drag either edge, double-click a section header, and the ordinary shortcuts
documentation.f6b5ea7d: Where a dropped file lives. Dragging spools the file to your temp folder and hands your DAW the path. A dropped .mid is copied into your project by every DAW, so those are cleaned up after a week; a dropped .wav is referenced by path, so those are never deleted — use your DAW's Collect All and Save to keep one for good.
documentation.f7ca8294: Proprietary, All Rights Reserved; the source code is private. You may not redistribute it or ship derivatives. It is not open source.
documentation.f8ac4ea5: Leave the seed box empty to get a fresh one each time; the chip then shows the seed that was actually used, so you can copy a generation you liked even though you never typed a number.
documentation.f8d5c8c2: Most MIDI generators think in genres. "Trap" is not "Metro Boomin," and no mainstream tool has heard of OsamaSon. Freally MIDI Master thinks in artists — each one a set of hand-authored style parameters describing hat-roll grammar, 808 slide behaviour, swing, register and section layout.
documentation.fa02d276: Are the artists involved? Did they approve this?
documentation.fb11f8c2: Drag a box to select cells
documentation.fb858c80: And it reports no project tempo unless you ask for one. Without --tempo there is no project, so nothing overrides the artist: pick a model and you hear it at the tempo it was authored at. Pass --tempo and that fixed value behaves exactly as a host's would.
documentation.fdbefea1: Pick someone. Type a name into the roster box — artists and genres alike.
features.036b5f21.b: Every other product on that table is asking you for money to do part of what this does. This one asks for nothing and does all of it.
features.05de2492: Lock it, reroll it, get it back
features.0b765e69: Stated plainly, because a feature list that hides its gaps is not worth reading.
features.0cdb36f4: Freally MIDI Master with a trap melody generated: the drum pads across the top, the piano roll and its velocity lane, the four Re-Dream clips under it, and the on-screen keyboard along the bottom.
features.11963ece: MIDI file → split into five parts, each explaining why
features.177ce0e6: 2,413 artists, producers and genres in one box — through aliases and past typos. Before you press a thing it tells you what that selection does: its era, its tempo range, the key it leans toward, its moods by name, and which parts it writes and which it does not. An artist who does not write countermelodies says so, instead of answering that tab with silence.
features.1cc2b417: Hook screening — refuses somebody else's melody
features.1ef3563d: A generated trap melody, its velocity lane, the four Re-Dreams of it, and the keyboard you can play it in from.
features.215a67ab: Built-in synth you can also just play
features.2cb5ea83: Train a style on takes you starred
features.2fb7a96e: It is free today. All of it.
features.3311e0fb: macOS and Linux drag-out are written and switched on but have not been dropped into a real DAW yet. Windows has. Export works everywhere regardless.
features.3f42ac73: And you can play it in
features.3f4902cc: Comparison compiled from each product's publicly documented feature set; products change, and corrections are welcome.
features.489d6eaf: Nothing was trained on anybody's recordings, because nothing was trained at all. The research corpus only ever contributed distributions — never note data, never audio.
features.512c7b09: The most complete MIDI generator ever built — and it costs nothing.
features.5916033f: Full song arrangement on an editable timeline
features.5a6369dd: Drag any sample — WAV, AIFF, FLAC, MP3, M4A, OGG — onto a generator and it comes back as notes. Onsets, tempo, the loop's own length, pitch and drum content, all measured. And every part tells you why it was routed where it was, so a wrong guess is one click to redirect rather than something you find out later.
features.5a67578e: Works fully offline, no account, no telemetry
features.5c924fb6: A polyphonic synthesiser with 1,648 instruments across 69 genres, and each melodic generator plays its own — four voices at once, not one shared between them. Nothing is a sample library: every sound is a five-integer address, so the whole thing is a few numbers in your project file.
features.5e30071b: Every figure here is counted from the shipping product and its test suite. Nothing is estimated, and nothing is rounded up.
features.65a59ac5: Search a name, not a genre
features.68dac5bc: Factory Packs: melodies, basslines, chords, countermelodies, drum loops and percussion loops, by genre. Walk them with ↑/↓ and each one plays as you land on it. Drag one onto a generator and it lands there, split onto the right parts; drag it out and it goes to your DAW as a clip. Nine megabytes of notes — not a gigabyte of somebody else's recordings, because our own generators and our own models wrote every one of them.
features.6b604c8e: Every feature, for everyone. No paid tier, no licence key, no in-app purchase, no subscription, no trial that expires, no "Pro" version holding the good parts hostage. That is written into this version's licence agreement: "The Software is provided free of charge, in full." And the music you make with it is yours, with no royalty and no attribution requirement.
features.6fe61d69: Song Mode: a whole arrangement on a timeline you can edit, one clip per part, each with its own MIDI and audio to drag out.
features.7142b88f.b: It is measured, not marketing. The test suite renders 200 seeds per model and measures 199 distinct Re-Dreams out of 200 draws from a single take. Neither number runs out at 200 samples, so both are floors: ≥200 generations × ≥199 Re-Dreams ≈ 40,000 takes per model per part, and 40,000 × 2,413 models is over 96 million — per part, before the four melodic parts combine. We report a floor and never a total, deliberately: a total would be a ceiling the code cannot prove, and it would turn inspiration that does not run out into a catalogue you can imagine finishing.
features.75b8dd39: The same seed gives the same notes, today and in five years. Nothing trained can promise that.
features.75f1827c: Reproducible seeds — paste it, get it back
features.77e297a3: Every melody is screened against a table of well-known contours before you hear it, and a take that matches is thrown away and drawn again. The table holds one-way fingerprints and no note data at all — transposing a hook does not hide it, and nothing anybody else wrote is in the product.
features.79dacbd4: Side by side with the leading MIDI generators
features.7a359bb4: Global hotkeys, screen share and camera in collaboration rooms.
features.8347a3e6: Lock what you like and reroll the rest — a locked lane comes back note for note however many times you press Generate. Every generation has a seed: copy it, paste it, get it back. And unlimited undo across everything, because an undo entry is the inputs rather than the notes.
features.891ee051: Your own samples on any lane
features.8d02c9f7: Every generation can tell you which parameter produced it, because there is a parameter rather than a weight.
features.94aff5cf: No account, no login, no telemetry, no cloud round-trip. It works on a plane. Your samples, your MIDI, your playing and your projects never leave your disk — not one sample byte crosses the wire, even in a collaboration room.
features.99073b05: It will not hand you somebody else's hook
features.b9301e2e: A reroll gives you a different idea. A Re-Dream gives you the same one, differently. Every generation arrives as four — the take you have, plus three dreamed after it — and you hear each one in your track, against your drums and your 808. A Re-Dream shares 79% of its original's onsets where three fresh seeds share 35%. That is a gate in the test suite, not a claim. It works on a file too: pick a .mid in the browser and the rack fills from that instead of from a generation.
features.b9fcfc0e: An on-screen keyboard, your computer keys as a second one, and your own MIDI controller with a channel filter, transpose, octave, bend range and a velocity curve. Press record and what you play lands in the part's clip — a note held across the end of the loop stays one note, and recording again overdubs rather than replacing. The pitch wheel bends every instrument, the physically modelled ones included: a bell's partials and a guitar's string move with it, while the parts that do not follow a note — a violin's body, a voice's formants — stay where they belong.
features.c9427ee1: Compiled from each product's own published feature set.
features.d19d4e76: 2,413 artist and producer styles. 1,648 instruments. Over 96 million distinct takes per part. Turn any audio file into MIDI. Re-Dream any idea into four. Arrange a whole song. Every feature, for everyone, free today.
features.d452e239: Why it is built the way it is
features.dacd8e46: Song Mode: a 56-bar arrangement on a timeline, with INTRO, VERSE, HOOK and OUTRO sections and one editable clip per part — drums, chords, melody and countermelody — each carrying its own MIDI and Audio chip.
features.ddfa7bdc: Lock what you like, reroll the rest
features.e3a8277a: The plugin reads the host's tempo and time signature every block, so a pattern is generated for your song — trap authored at 140 comes out at 92 in a 92 BPM project. Pin a tempo yourself and yours wins.
features.f28580e7: Not a limitation — the design. Rules, measurements and seeded randomness all the way down, with a build gate that refuses any dependency that would smuggle a model in. It buys you reproducibility, explainability, and provenance you can defend: nothing was trained on anybody's recordings, because nothing was trained at all.
features.f3789702: 5,085 MIDI loops, written by the same engine
features.fa2456cd: v1.0.0RC is coming soon, and downloads with it. Until then the honest answer to "where do I get it" is not yet.
features.fbe4c84f: Drums · Melody · Countermelody · Bassline · Chords — plus Song Mode, which samples one of the artist's own forms and draws it on a timeline you can edit. Resize, clone, lock what you like, reroll a section without touching the rest.

honest.title: The things most sites put at the bottom
index.06309989: No file to drag, no folder to hunt for. The plugin emits MIDI where you inserted it, in the host's own time.
index.0e16857e: Drums, melodies, countermelodies, 808s, chords and full song arrangements — generated in the style of specific artists, as original MIDI, in your project's own key and tempo. Free, offline, and 100% AI-free.
index.1497b93b.b: A page has to be fetched — the app itself, and the style data it generates from. That is the whole of it. Generation runs on your own machine, in your own browser; your beats, your seeds and anything you import stay there and are never uploaded. After one visit the tab works with the network switched off, which is closer to offline than most software manages.
index.1497b93b.t: The web app is delivered over the network; what you make is not
index.21393e5c: No models, no training data, no inference, and no network calls during generation. No login and no telemetry. Everything happens on your machine — including "train your own style", which measures the takes you kept and writes the numbers back rather than learning anything. A build with an AI or an HTTP client anywhere in its dependencies fails the build.
index.2419a115.b: With no royalty and no attribution requirement. Freally MIDI Master itself is proprietary, All Rights Reserved, and its source code is private — you may not redistribute it. It is not open source.
index.2419a115.t: The music you make with it is yours
index.25a8716e: The engine is rule-based, not trained
index.276d670e: Build a style of your own
index.3bb0362b: Every generation has a seed. Copy it, paste it, get the exact same beat back — on any machine, on any day. Determinism is enforced by the test suite.
index.40df2f36.b: Rooms connect your machine directly to the people you invite. If you save someone as a buddy, a small service can tell you when they are online — and it is told nothing worth knowing: a key that changes every few minutes, and an address encrypted to a secret only the two of you hold. It cannot read it, cannot list who is there, and cannot work out who knows whom. Turn it off, or never save a buddy, and you paste a code instead — which is how rooms work anyway.
index.40df2f36.t: Collaboration is the one exception, and only if you use it
index.420c17ef: Most generators think in genres. "Trap" is not "Metro Boomin," and no mainstream tool has heard of OsamaSon. Type a name and get patterns carrying that artist's actual signatures.
index.4c860bcf: Freally MIDI Master began as a desktop app; v0.2.0 was that build. As of 29 July 2026 the desktop app is retired — it is no longer built or released. Nothing already installed stops working; it simply stops finding updates.
index.644f2e23: There is no AI in this product. No models, no training data, no inference, no network calls during generation. The engine is deterministic procedural code reading hand-authored style parameters derived from published research. That is a legal architecture as much as a technical one: nothing here is copied MIDI, sampled audio, or a transcription of anyone's record, and there is no feature that recreates a specific song. Artist names are descriptive style references only.
index.6a3c2dd2.b: The two that used to exist — a launch-time update check and an opt-in crash report — belonged to the desktop app and were removed with it. A plugin is installed and updated by whoever installs plugins. Enforced by two build gates rather than promised: no HTTP client is compiled into the plugin — still true, because the collaboration service is reached by a separate program, never by the plugin your DAW loads — and the interface itself is driven through a generation on every commit and fails if it attempts a single request off the machine. Crash reports are written to your own disk and never sent anywhere.
index.6a3c2dd2.t: The plugin makes no outbound connections at all
index.7e9d277b: Artist and producer names in Freally MIDI Master are descriptive references to a musical style, nothing more. No affiliation, endorsement, or authorship is implied or claimed. Every pattern is generated procedurally from hand-authored style parameters — no MIDI, audio, or data is copied from any recording. All trademarks and names are the property of their respective owners. Read the full disclaimer.
index.84153fc4: Start from any artist, adjust what you care about, and save it — it sits in the roster beside the shipped ones and works exactly the same, because it is the same kind of thing. Star the takes you like and it fits a style to them.
index.986fa10d: It is now a CLAP plugin, with VST3 and AU projected from it — not for the format's sake, but because a plugin is handed the host's tempo, time signature and playhead. A generated pattern lands in the song you are actually writing, instead of at whatever tempo the artist happens to be authored at.
index.99276787: Every build lands a whole capability. Nothing ships half-done.
index.a4c6de24: No accounts. No telemetry. Nothing about you, your projects or your output is ever transmitted. Generation, playback, import and export are entirely local.
index.a9e41a1f: Status — it is a plugin now
index.b5d5c2d0.b: The collaboration feature — rooms, in development and not installed by anything today — needs to learn your machine's public address before two people can connect directly, which is what a STUN server is for. When it lands, opening or joining a room will contact one; this build names Cloudflare and Google. Such a server learns only that some address is using a WebRTC application — not who you are talking to, and not what you send — and nothing is contacted until you open or join a room. The sentence above stays true for the plugin as it ships today.
index.b5d5c2d0.t: One thing that is coming, said now rather than when it ships
index.bab9531a: The plugin reads the host's tempo and time signature every block, so trap authored at 140 comes out at 92 in a 92 BPM project. Pin a tempo and yours wins instead.
index.bd395814: Drums, Melody, Countermelody, Bassline and Chords — plus Song Mode, which is not a sixth generator but an arrangement that fills all five in.
index.daba7f83: There is nothing to download yet. v1.0.0RC is next, and it is being tested by hand right now — every host, every OS, and the things no test suite can judge. A plugin that half-works inside somebody's session is worse than one that is not there, so it ships when that matrix is green and not before.
index.e46c4677: It loads and generates in Ableton Live 12 (VST3) and FL Studio (CLAP). Reaper, Bitwig and Logic are not yet tested. The standalone build runs the same plugin in its own window with no DAW involved.
index.efa5276f: Pick a mood and stay there, or leave it on Any and let each press walk that artist's range. One artist writes more than one kind of record, and no seed could ever cross between them.
index.f52c92c0: No AI, no account, no cloud
ladder.rung.v0.3.0: Plugin pivot. CLAP, with VST3 and AU projected from it. Loads in Ableton and FL Studio.
ladder.rung.v0.4.0: Unlimited undo. Every session change, one keystroke back — no depth limit.
ladder.rung.v0.5.0: It makes a sound. A sampler behind the generators, your own one-shots on any part, and a transport that plays inside the plugin.
ladder.rung.v0.5.5: It plays an instrument. A synthesizer behind every part, a factory library of 2,729,088 sounds you can browse by instrument and genre, a sample-pack maker, and a keyboard you can play at any time.
ladder.rung.v0.5.7: A vast, ultra-realistic library. Twenty-four new synthesis engines and 750 new instruments — 975 in all, from concert grands and bowed sections to modelled analog circuits — each one measured against the real thing it is named for. 1,614,600 sounds, and still not one file on your disk.
ladder.rung.v0.6.0: Your sample library. A folder tree with preview, starred favourites, drag-to-pad and reverse — plus drop a MIDI file in and it works out which parts are in it.
ladder.rung.v0.7.0: The arrangement, like a DAW. Clips drawn from their own notes, zoom, multi-select, trim and clone — and drag the whole song out, one track per part.
ladder.rung.v0.8.0: 67 genres, 2,000 artists. The full roster — the underground beside the mainstream — every one a hand-written style model. The 67 genres are written and so are 1,250 artists and producers; the rest are being encoded from the research a volume at a time.
ladder.rung.v0.9.0: Polish and hardening. Every state designed and every edge handled: accessibility, HiDPI, crash safety, cold start under three seconds.
ladder.rung.v1.0.0: Downloads open. All five generators plus Song Mode, collaboration rooms and MixSir, every format, on all three platforms. The first build anyone can install — after an optimization pass, a simplification pass, a code review and a security review, with both self-hosted CI runners green.
ladder.rung.v1.0.0-beta: Feature complete. Everything 1.0 promises, plus collaboration rooms and Freally MixSir, the phone companion. Still no download — this is the build that gets tested by hand.
ladder.rung.v1.0.0RC: Release candidate. Re-Dream lands — every generation arrives as four, the take you have plus three dreamed after it, auditioned in the track before one replaces the part. Then the manual test pass, worked end to end on real hardware in a real DAW.
roster.827703c6: Every artist, producer and genre the plugin models.
roster.8d0c67df: These are hand-authored parameters, not training data. Nobody's audio was analysed to build any of this. Each entry is a set of numbers a human wrote down from published research — tempo ranges, swing, which beats a kick lands on — and the names are used the way a genre name is used, to say what a style sounds like. There is no model trained on anyone here, and the plugin generates original patterns rather than reproducing any recording.
